label: group chat
lines: maya: ok that video actually explained the whole click-to-webpage thing pretty well 👀
dev: right?? like the internet has literally no single owner, it's just a giant network of computers running on shared standards
sam: and every device gets there through wifi or cellular first, then the router hands it off to your isp
maya: also every device has its own ip address, either ipv4 or ipv6, so data knows where to go
dev: and the data doesn't even travel whole, it gets chopped into packets that take different routes and get reassembled at the end
sam: those packets ride on the actual backbone too, fiber and undersea cables connecting cities and continents, isps help maintain that
maya: then when you type an address, dns kicks in as the 'phone book' and turns it into an ip address in milliseconds
dev: after that your device hits the web server, gets the files back, and your browser builds the page with html, css and js 💻
sam: don't forget the security stuff — https encrypts the connection, firewalls filter traffic, vpns hide your ip, and malware/phishing are the everyday risks
maya: it also covered daily use stuff like email, buffered video streaming, cloud storage, social media, e-commerce and search all running on the same infrastructure
dev: plus protocols like tcp/ip, http, ftp, smtp letting systems talk, and bandwidth/latency shaping how fast it feels
sam: and it ended on governance and the future — net neutrality, icann, ietf, w3c, then teased 5g, ai and quantum computing next 🚀
